Based on the camera orientation and the captured images, we create a point cloud. The point cloud is quite rough and only consists of points in 3D space and no colour. Based on the point cloud information, a mesh is created. This mesh, or \"lump of clay\", is what we will bring to the next stage of the process: the sculpting.

The first part of the scanning is the calibration step. As you circulate slowly around the object, the camera takes images of the object. The algorithm at work looks for things that stand out in the images. Anything that can be identified and saved as a feature of the object or the surrounding environment, is a feature point. Feature points are used to calculate where the camera is located in the room in relation to the scanned object.

Lastly, the app creates the texture. The texture in this context refers to the colours of the object. Using a few of the images captured during the sculpting, the colours are projected onto the mesh from different perspectives.
